trickyParts: release() is idempotent via a `released` flag: index.ts releases through stop() on a failed boot probe and again in startDaemon's catch; a bare second closeSync would throw EBADF (or close a reused descriptor number).

O_CLOEXEC is the numeric per-platform constant (Linux 0o2000000, Darwin 0x1000000): fs.constants.O_CLOEXEC is undefined under Bun 1.3.14 and Bun's openSync does not set it; the no-inherit test asserts the bit via /proc/self/fdinfo on Linux.
errno is read immediately after the failed flock, before closeSync, via __errno_location through bun:ffi; a losing contender closes its descriptor before the bounded pid re-read (20 x 25 ms).

corrective.trigger: tester finding F1 (.legion/test.json; https://github.com/sjawhar/legion/pull/1004#issuecomment-5651797778): 'is never inherited by a spawned process: the descriptor is close-on-exec' flaky 3/150 file loops, 1/2 full suites
corrective.rootCause: Bun.spawn vforks; the child marks inherited fds CLOEXEC via close_range and relies on execve to close them; the kernel resumes the vfork parent from exec_mmap(), before do_close_on_exec(), so Bun.spawn can return while the child still holds a dup of the lock descriptor. flock is per open file description, so release() drops nothing until that dup closes. Test predicate was wrong; module untouched.

Extracted `firstLine(child, role)` shared with spawnHolder's 'locked' wait. Linux /proc/self/fdinfo CLOEXEC-bit assertion kept. No retries, no sleeps. instance-lock.ts unchanged.
